text:
maya: FYI — partial-quant canary from this morning is showing a runtime / latency drift on long context runs (8k tokens). p99 up ~18% vs baseline.

devon: ugh. which kernel path is firing? INT8 fallback somewhere? link to trace?

maya: quick summary pasted from perf-runner: p50 +3%, p95 +12%, p99 +18%. GPU timeline shows lots of micro-kernel launches around layer 3-6 during kv-append. KV cache latency spikes correlate with those micro-kernels.

sanjay: can you paste the kernel selection decision log for a single request? curious whether selector oscillates between INT8 and FP8 per-layer.

maya: log snippet:
```
[selector] layer=2 choose=int8 latency_est=0.9ms qual_delta=0.002
[selector] layer=3 choose=fp8 latency_est=1.2ms qual_delta=-0.001
[selector] layer=4 choose=int8 latency_est=0.95ms qual_delta=0.003
[kv] cache_append latency=2.3ms
[selector] layer=5 choose=int8 latency_est=0.89ms qual_delta=0.004
[kv] cache_read latency=3.1ms
```
Seems like the selector is flipping a lot mid-request (int8 <-> fp8).

zara: that kind of oscillation can cause dispatcher thrash — kernel launch overhead + different workspace sizes = lots of small copies. Also quant calibration stats might be stale per layer.

devon: are embeddings and lm_head excluded in this canary? we usually exclude them for safety.

maya: Yes embeddings and lm_head were excluded. The oddity is some middle layers (3,4) are marked sensitive by the calibration pass for this model and got forced to fp8, but adjacent layers chose int8.

ci-bot: New perf trace uploaded: https://internal/traces/1748881234/scanstage-canary (artifact TTL 7d) :mag:

sanjay: two quick proposals: 1) add hysteresis to kernel selector so it doesn't flip for N tokens within a single request; 2) bias calibration stats to prefer wider-type when adjacent layers differ — that reduces mode switches.

devon: +1 on hysteresis. Also we should try grouping requests by (model, kv_state_signature) in the batcher so kernels are consistent across the micro-batch (reduce mixed kernel launches).

maya: prototype per-request override config I tested locally:
```
{
  "quantization": {
    "default": "int8",
    "overrides": [
      { "layer_idx": 0, "prec": "fp16", "reason": "embed" },
      { "layer_idx": -1, "prec": "fp16", "reason": "lm_head" },
      { "layer_idx": 3, "prec": "fp16", "reason": "sensitivity_scan(v1)" }
    ],
    "selector_hysteresis_tokens": 32
  }
}
```
This reduced p99 by ~9% on my local run, but we saw a small BLEU drop on a subset eval for a few prompts (layer 3 fp16 might be borderline).

zara: can we instead mark layer 3 as "soft-exclude" in routing — selector prefers fp16 but will stay int8 if neighbor layers are int8 and quality delta < threshold? that might avoid quality regress + perf thrash.

sanjay: agree. Also adjust the calibration window: don't use last-N-tokens global stat; use per-layer representative batches sampled from PROD-like sequences (long context). Current calibrator was trained on short chatlike samples.

devon: micro-batching note: change batcher key from (model, dtype) to (model, dtype, kv_hash_prefix) so we don't mix cold vs warm KV cache requests in the same micro-batch — mixing causes different workspace sizes and kernel choices.

maya: good call. I ran the change to batching key + selector_hysteresis together: p99 improved and kernel-launch count dropped ~40%. Quality diffs reduced to noise except a few hard prompts.

zara: we should automate sensitivity labeling: run the per-layer micro-eval (500 examples) and mark any layer with >0.5% quality delta as "sensitive" and add it to the soft-exclude list. That way we avoid manual tuning.

ci-bot: Perf alert: regression ticket created -> PERF-4872 (assignee: devon).

devon: I'll own the hysteresis + batcher key change, and add an A/B canary across 10% traffic with long-context traces.

maya: action items:
- devon: implement selector_hysteresis + batcher key change (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- sanjay: update calibrator to sample long-context reps (ETA 2d)
- zara: add automated sensitivity scan job and label exporter (ETA 3d)
- maya: run Canary + eval suite on 10% traffic (start when devon finishes)

zara: also add telemetry metric: kernel_switches_per_request and kv_cache_coalesce_ratio. will help detect regressions early.

devon: noted. creating PR for the selector hysteresis now -> https://git/repo/pulls/4123 :rocket:

maya: thanks. ping here when PR is merged and I will kick off the canary. :thumbsup:

sanjay: one more note — watch out for quant calibration causing perf to get better but quality to degrade on tail prompts. add per-prompt rollback thresholds in the reroute policy.

maya: yes — we will gate by both perf and eval-quality metrics. moving to follow-up thread for rollout details.

devon: merging PR in 20m.
